lines: Six-month history of irregular menstrual cycles ranging from 21 to 60 days apart and difficulty conceiving

This 32-year-old female with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus, Hashimoto's thyroiditis, and primary adrenal insufficiency diagnosed in January 2020 presents to Obstetrics and Gynecology with menstrual irregularity and fertility concerns.
She reports her menstrual cycles have become increasingly sporadic, ranging from 21 to 60 days apart, and she has not had a period for the past 3 months.
She also complains of hot flashes, night sweats, and vaginal dryness.
Her past medical history is significant for Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
She takes for which she takes levothyroxine.
- Insulin glargine 22 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin aspart sliding scale 1:15 ratio with meals
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO every morning, 10 mg PO every afternoon
- Sumatriptan 50 mg PO as needed for migraine (max 200 mg/day)
She denies any family history of early menopause or autoimmune diseases.
On physical examination, her vital signs are within normal limits
Her thyroid gland is non-tender and of normal size.
A pelvic examination reveals no abnormalities.

encounters.cc: Sudden episode of unresponsiveness with lip smacking witnessed by husband

lines: Sudden episode of unresponsiveness with lip smacking witnessed by husband

The patient is a 35-year-old female with a known history of temporal lobe epilepsy, Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus, and primary adrenal insufficiency who was evaluated three months ago for recurrent adrenal insufficiency symptoms and is brought to the emergency department by her husband after experiencing a sudden episode of unresponsiveness while cooking dinner.
The husband reports that she stopped talking mid-sentence, stared blankly, and began smacking her lips repeatedly.
She did not respond to her name being called and did not recall the event afterward.
The episode lasted for about 2 minutes, and she appeared confused for an additional 10 minutes post-event.
Her past medical history is significant for type 1 diabetes mellitus and migraines.
Her medications include insulin glargine, insulin aspart, and sumatriptan as needed.
- Hydrocortisone 20 mg PO every morning, 10 mg PO every afternoon
On examination, she is alert and oriented but reports a mild headache and fatigue.
Her blood glucose level at the time of the examination is 98 mg/dL.
An electroencephalogram (EEG) shows focal epileptiform discharges in the left temporal lobe.
